newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria keeps trade guessing on durum import plan.
newsitem.headline: Algeria keeps trade guessing on durum import plan.

text.p: European grain traders were in the dark on Thursday over the outcome of an Algerian tender for the import of 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat.
Several traders said that although there was disagreement over prices, Algeria might still be negotiating with exporters.
But others suggested Algeria might have already passed on offers because the prices were too high.
Others were trying to get to the bottom of market talk that Algeria might already have bought two to four cargoes at prices ranging from $200 to $208 per tonne, including cost and freight,
"Until Wednesday talks were going on," said one trader.
He said Algeria might have passed on offers and decided to re-tender for the wheat at a later date.
Operators doubted they would get more details later on because most Algerian administrative offices were closed for business on Thursday.
Algeria was seeking the wheat for shipment between mid-March and end-April.
